subtitle: Out Manila · Cebu Pacific
overview: Five days across Tokyo, the Mt. Fuji area and Kamakura on a private-coach tour with an English-speaking guide. See Mt. Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi, try a matcha experience, shop at Gotemba Premium Outlets and enjoy dinner and an onsen at your Mt. Fuji hotel, then visit Kamakura’s Great Buddha, Asakusa and Shibuya Crossing. Fly Manila – Tokyo (Narita) and back with Cebu Pacific; stay in 4-star hotels.
travelDatesNote: Departures from Manila, Feb 13–17 2027 to Jun 23–27 2027. The rate changes by date: an amount on a date is added to the base rate per pax. Seats are limited and confirmed at booking.

placeDesc.Lake Kawaguchi: One of the Fuji Five Lakes, famed for reflections and views of Mt. Fuji.
placeDesc.Oshino Hakkai: A village of eight clear spring-fed ponds at the foot of Mt. Fuji, with traditional thatched houses.
placeDesc.Gotemba Premium Outlets: A large outlet mall near Mt. Fuji with Japanese and international brands and views of the mountain.
placeDesc.Great Buddha of Kamakura: A large outdoor bronze Buddha statue at Kotoku-in temple in Kamakura.
placeDesc.Komachi-dori: Kamakura's lively shopping street near the station, with sweets, snacks and souvenirs.
placeDesc.Asakusa Temple: Sensoji, Tokyo's oldest temple, reached through the Kaminarimon gate and Nakamise shopping street.
placeDesc.Tokyo Skytree: Tokyo's tall broadcasting tower near Asakusa, seen here on a photo stop.
placeDesc.Shibuya Crossing: The famous busy pedestrian scramble crossing in front of Shibuya Station.
placeDesc.Hachiko Statue: A bronze statue of the loyal dog Hachiko outside Shibuya Station, a popular meeting spot.
placeDesc.Meiji Shrine: A Shinto shrine in a forested park in Tokyo, dedicated to Emperor Meiji and his wife.
placeDesc.Shinjuku: Tokyo's busy district of shops, restaurants and neon, visited on the shopping street.
